chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who married a woman but did not enter (consume) with her, so she claimed that her dower was one hundred dinars, and the husband mentioned that her dower was fifty dinars, and there was no proof between them, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The word is the word of the husband with his oath.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a husband and wife disagree on the amount of the dower and there is no proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of 'al-qawl qawl al-zawj ma'a yaminih' (the husband's word prevails with his oath) in cases of conflicting claims regarding the dower (mahr) without witnesses. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving evidentiary gaps by prioritizing the party with the stronger initial claim or possession, here the husband, provided he substantiates it with an oath. This ruling underscores the importance of oaths in Islamic civil law as a decisive proof when documentary evidence is absent.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

regarding a man who married a woman but did not copulate with her. So she claims that her dower was of one hundred Dinars, and the husband mentions that her dower was of fifty Dinars, and there is no proof between the two of them. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The (final) word is the word of the husband with a swear (of an oath)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from abu ‘Ubaydah who has said the following: “About the case of a man who marries a woman but he does not go to bed with her and she claims that her mahr (dower) is one hundred dinar while the husband says that it is fifty dinar and there is no witness, abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The words of the husband are accepted on oath.’”
